skills.grammarMd:
Ask **Karê te çi ye?** What is your job? — *Ez mamoste me.* I am a teacher.

Many jobs are built from a word and an ending:

- **-kar / -ker**: *cot* plough → *cotkar* farmer · *kar* work → *karker* worker
- **-van**: *rojname* newspaper → *rojnamevan* journalist · *şivan* shepherd
- **-dar**: *dikan* shop → *dikandar* shopkeeper
- **-pêj**: *aşpêj* cook · *nanpêj* baker

To say what someone **becomes**, use *bûn*: *Ez dixwazim bibim mamoste.* I want to become a teacher. · *Ew bû endezyar.* She became an engineer.

Where: *Ew li nexweşxaneyê dixebite.* He works at the hospital.

skills.grammarMd:
For what **has happened** (and still matters), add the copula-like endings to the past stem:

- after a consonant: *ez hatime, tu hatiyî, ew hatiye, em hatine* (I have come …)
- after a vowel: *ez çûme, tu çûyî, ew çûye, em çûne* (I have gone …)
- verbs in -în: *ez hizirîme, ew hiziriye* (I have thought …)

Transitive verbs keep the ergative: *Min biryar daye.* I have decided. · *Te hîç Hewlêr dîtiye?* Have you ever seen Hewlêr? · *Me sêv xwarine.* We have eaten (the) apples.

Useful with it: **tu car**, **tu caran** never · **hîç** ever (in a question), at all · **heta niha** until now · **hê** / **hîn** still, yet: *Ez hê neçûme.* I have not gone yet.

Not: *ne-* before the stem: *Min nedîtiye.* I haven’t seen it.

new.en: has …ed (the present perfect: min daye, ew hatiye)

skills.grammarMd:
Join two thoughts with these:

- **ji ber ku / çimkî** because: *Ez diçim, ji ber ku ev derfeteke mezin e.* I am going because this is a big chance.
- **loma / ji ber vê yekê** so, that is why: *Baran ditirse, loma Hamo alîkariya wî dike.* Baran is afraid, so Hamo helps him.
- **lê / lêbelê** but, however: *Hewlêr dûr e, lê ez ê her Newrozê bêm.* Hewlêr is far, but I will come every Newroz.
- **hem … hem** both … and: *Ew hem mamoste ye hem jî nivîskar.* She is both a teacher and a writer.
- **bêyî ku** + subjunctive, without: *bêyî ku bihizire* without thinking
- **her çend** although: *Her çend ez ditirsim jî, ez ê biçim.* Although I am afraid, I will go.

skills.grammarMd:
For plans and hopes the subjunctive comes back after **ku**:

- *Hêvî dikim ku tu serkeftî bî.* I hope that you will be successful.
- *Armanca min ev e ku ez zimanê dayikê hînî zarokan bikim.* My goal is to teach children their mother tongue.

**dema ku** + subjunctive talks about the future: *Dema ku ez biçim Hewlêrê, ez ê her roj telefonî we bikim.* When I go to Hewlêr, I will phone you every day.

And the plain future for what is decided: *Em ê bên serdana te.* We will come to visit you.

Wishes for the road: *Bi xêr biçî!* Go well! · *Serkeftin!* Good luck!

payload.title: Telefonek ji Kobaniyê re

lines.text: Xalo, Xezal li ber dîwarê baxçe ye. Ew digirî.
lines.en: Uncle, Xezal is by the orchard wall. She’s crying.

lines.text: Ez dizanim. Ew ditirse ku ji gund, ji zarokên xwe yên dibistanê û ji min dûr bikeve.
lines.en: I know. She’s afraid of being far from the village, from her schoolchildren, and from me.

lines.text: Û tu çi jê re dibêjî?
lines.en: And what are you telling her?

lines.text: Ez? Tiştekî nabêjim. Ez telefonî bavê xwe dikim.
lines.en: Me? Nothing. I’m phoning my father.

lines.text: Bavê te? Li Kobaniyê?
lines.en: Your father? In Kobanî?

lines.text: Bavo, Xezal li vir e. Tu dikarî bi wê re biaxivî?
lines.en: Dad, Xezal is here. Can you talk to her?

lines.text: Ew çi dibêje? Dengê wî nayê.
lines.en: What is he saying? I can’t hear his voice.

lines.text: Ew dibêje: «Roja ku Hamo ji Kobaniyê çû, min jê re got…»
lines.en: He says: “The day Hamo left Kobanî, I told him…”

lines.text: «Here, lê rehên xwe ji bîr meke.»
lines.en: “Go, but don’t forget your roots.”

lines.text: Binêre! Xezal dikene û digirî, herdu bi hev re.
lines.en: Look! Xezal is laughing and crying, both at once.

lines.text: Û tu, xalo? Tu jî digirî?
lines.en: And you, uncle? Are you crying too?

lines.text: Na, na… çavên min pîr in.
lines.en: No, no… my eyes are old.

payload.title: Evîn jî reh e

lines.text: Xalo, tu çima ji Kobaniyê hatî Sêvanê?
lines.en: Uncle, why did you come from Kobanî to Sêvan?

lines.text: Ji ber ku havînên min ên zarokatiyê li vir derbas bûn.
lines.en: Because the summers of my childhood were spent here.

lines.text: Tenê ji ber vê yekê?
lines.en: Only for that reason?

lines.text: Û ji ber ku sêvên Sêvanê ji yên Kobaniyê şîrîntir in!
lines.en: And because the apples of Sêvan are sweeter than Kobanî’s!

lines.text: Xalo! Ev ne reh in, ev sêv in!
lines.en: Uncle! Those aren’t roots, those are apples!

lines.text: Sêv jî ji rehan tên.
lines.en: Apples come from roots too.

lines.text: Û rehên te? Li ku ne?
lines.en: And your roots? Where are they?

lines.text: Rehên min li Kobaniyê ne. Hêza min jî ji wir tê.
lines.en: My roots are in Kobanî. My strength comes from there too.

lines.text: Lê sî sal e tu li vir î.
lines.en: But you’ve been here for thirty years.

lines.text: Erê. Ji ber dilgermiya mirovên Sêvanê ez li vir mam.
lines.en: Yes. Because of the warmth of Sêvan’s people, I stayed.

lines.text: Ango evîn jî reh e?
lines.en: So love is a root too?

lines.text: Belê. Rehê herî bihêz.
lines.en: Yes. The strongest root of all.
